checks.ref:
command:. .gnomish/lib/task-change.sh
review="$reports/review-code.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-code stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: Severity understated: R1 is a WARNING, yet the review itself marks tasks 7.4, 8.2 and 11.3 ❌, and all three are ticked [x] in tasks.md. 7.4 says 'split the steps file if it passes 200 lines' (settings_language_unit.steps.tsx has 279), 8.2 says 'split into InterfaceLanguageGroup.keyboard.test.tsx if it passes 200 lines' (the file has 254), and 11.3 requires 'wc -l of every new or changed file under src/ is under 200', a check that fails. The acceptance criteria name 'a ticked-but-undone task' as a CRITICAL case, so R1 should be CRITICAL. The review's 'No user-visible behaviour is affected' does not override that.

The verdict is inconsistent with the findings: it says 'Ready. No CRITICAL finding blocks the change: every requirement and scenario is implemented and tested', while the Tasks section reports 40/43 with three ticked tasks failing their own stated conditions. Once R1 is graded correctly, the verdict should not be Ready until the files are split (or the task text is honestly reconciled) and tasks 7.4/8.2/11.3 match.
